blocks.content: To promote old age income security by establishing, developing and regulating pension funds, and to protect the interests of subscribers to schemes of pension funds.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: PFRDA was established to promote old age income security by establishing, developing, and regulating pension funds in India.
It acts as a statutory regulatory body protecting the interests of subscribers to schemes of pension funds.
PFRDA regulates and administers both the National Pension System (NPS) and the Atal Pension Yojana (APY).
It oversees key intermediaries including Pension Fund Managers, Central Recordkeeping Agencies (CRAs), and Points of Presence (PoPs).
PFRDA was constituted initially in 2003 by a executive resolution and attained statutory status under the PFRDA Act, 2013.
NPS is mandatory for all Central Government employees joining service on or after January 1, 2004 (excluding Armed Forces).
Atal Pension Yojana (APY) targets unorganised sector workers within the entry age group of 18 to 40 years.
